title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Choppy shore break after Thursday's AI wipeout
conditions.summary: Tech futures are bouncing after Thursday's steep AI-led selloff, but Dow futures, crypto and Asia are still under water. The October jobs report at 7:30 AM CT is the big set of the day.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: Nasdaq-100 futures are up about 1.2% and S&P 500 futures about 0.2% in early trading, while Dow futures are down about 0.9% and Russell futures are flat; early quotes can shift.
Thursday was rough: the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq 5.5%, its deepest one-day drop in about 19 months, pushing it into correction territory.
The selloff was blamed on fears that Democratic control of Congress after the midterms could bring tougher AI rules and slower data-center buildout, plus higher oil feeding rate-hike worries.
The VIX is easing to about 26 after Thursday's biggest one-day jump in roughly 19 months.
The 10-year Treasury yield slipped to about 4.84%; the dollar index sits near 101.7.
WTI crude is near $90, down slightly after jumping Thursday on tanker attacks and uncertain US-Iran talks; gold is down about 1% near $4,075.
Bitcoin is down about 5% near $76,000, hit by over $1 billion of leveraged liquidations and ETF outflows.
Asia: Japan's Nikkei and Korea's Kospi each fell about 6% in the latest session, with a circuit breaker halting Korean trading at the open.
Europe: early European figures were not available in our sources this morning.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: October jobs report. Consensus is roughly +59,000 to +65,000 payrolls after +29,000 in September; unemployment seen steady at 4.2%; hourly wages seen +0.3% month over month.
9:00 AM CT: Preliminary November University of Michigan consumer sentiment.
Fed: futures price roughly a two-in-three chance of a rate hike in December, so a hot jobs number could add pressure.
Earlier this week, ADP showed 86,000 private jobs added in October, above expectations.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Airbnb raised its full-year revenue growth forecast after Thursday's close; shares are up about 12% pre-market.
Cloudflare reported after Thursday's close and is up around 15% pre-market.
Atlassian is down about 16% pre-market after its first-quarter results.
Monster Beverage also reported after Thursday's close.
This morning: Enbridge, Humana and Vistra are among the companies reporting before the open.
No major reports are scheduled after today's close; next week brings Constellation Energy, CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: ABNB (Airbnb): +12% — raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth forecast.
NET (Cloudflare): about +15% — rallying after quarterly results released Thursday evening.
TEAM (Atlassian): -16% — shares slide after first-quarter results.
NVDA (Nvidia): +3.6% — bouncing after its biggest one-day drop since January 2025.
AMD, INTC, AVGO, MU (AMD, Intel, Broadcom, Micron): +5% to +8% — chipmakers rebound after Thursday's AI rout.
CRWV, NBIS, IREN, APLD (CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, Applied Digital): higher — AI data-center names recovering part of deep losses.
GEV, CEG (GE Vernova, Constellation Energy): higher — power-for-AI plays steadying after Thursday's selloff.

sections.title: Business News
items: Defense-tech firm Shield AI agreed to buy radar maker Echodyne in a deal valued at up to $5.3 billion and raised $2.5 billion in new funding at a $28.8 billion valuation.
Adani Ports agreed to buy Dutch liquid storage operator Evos for an enterprise value of €2.56 billion, its big push into European terminals.
Alfa Laval agreed to buy maritime software firm NAVTOR for about $700 million.
Washington's new balance of power after the midterms is now a market story, with investors weighing what it means for AI regulation and data-center spending.
Oil stays jumpy on tanker attacks and stop-start US-Iran talks, keeping energy inflation on the radar.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT jobs report: a hot number could feed December rate-hike bets; a soft one could ease yields.
Whether the pre-market chip bounce holds after the 8:30 AM CT open, or Thursday's AI selling resumes.
VIX near 26 and bitcoin near $76,000 as gauges of risk appetite into the weekend.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, November sixth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the cabana deck is my co-anchor, Gus the wonder dog, nose up and sniffing the sea breeze. Give the crew a big Friday hello, Gus! Alright, the swell. Thursday was a gnarly wipeout. The S and P five hundred fell about four and a half percent, and the Nasdaq dropped five and a half percent, its worst day in about nineteen months, sliding into correction territory. The worry: tougher A I rules from the new Congress, plus higher oil. This Dawn Patrol, the water is mixed. Nasdaq one hundred futures are up about one point two percent, S and P futures up about two tenths of a percent, while Dow futures are down about nine tenths of a percent. The VIX eased to about twenty six, the ten year yield is about four point eight four percent, and bitcoin is down about five percent. Japan and Korea each fell about six percent. Now the wind and weather. The big set rolls in at seven thirty A M Central with the October jobs report. Forecasters expect around sixty thousand jobs, with unemployment at four point two percent. Consumer sentiment follows at nine A M Central. Traders see about a two in three chance of a Fed hike in December. On the tide chart, Airbnb raised its full year growth forecast and is up about twelve percent before the bell. Stoked to see it! That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Cloudflare is hanging ten too, up around fifteen percent after its results. Atlassian took a wipeout, down about sixteen percent after its quarterly report. In the lineup, the chip crowd is paddling back out. Nvidia is up about three and a half percent, and A M D, Intel, Broadcom and Micron are up five to eight percent. Beach talk. Shield A I agreed to buy radar maker Echodyne in a deal worth up to five point three billion dollars. Adani Ports is buying European storage operator Evos. Sets to watch: the jobs report, and whether the chip bounce holds after the eight thirty open. Soul surfers, remember, one rough day does not make a season. Want a read on a wave of your own?
